notes: Step 1 parts are unchanged: 1 Uno, 1 breadboard, 1 Memsic 2125, 6 hook-up wires (orange, blue, yellow, 3 black).

The sensor straddles the breadboard centre gap, with 3 pins in each half in columns 17, 18 and 19. The catalogue names the top half 't' (rows a-e) and the bottom half 'b' (rows f-j). So the image's top half is 't' and its bottom half is 'b'. The pins sit in the rows next to the gap: 't' row e and 'b' row f.

Pin mapping follows the schematic. Bottom row is col 17 GND.2, col 18 X out, col 19 +5V (VDD). Top row is col 17 GND.1, col 18 Y out, col 19 Temp (TOUT). Temp is left unconnected, as in the circuit image.
Signal wires: yellow goes from pin 2 to X out. Blue goes from pin 3 to Y out. This matches the tutorial text and the schematic.
The orange wire goes from Uno 5V to VDD, through the breadboard column 19 bottom strip.

The ground path is Uno GND.1, then a black wire to the bottom negative rail 'bn'. Two short black wires join that rail to the sensor's two GND columns. Rail hole numbers (5, 10, 13) are estimated from the picture and only matter in that they are on the same rail strip.
The ends of the black Uno GND wire and the 5V wire go to the Uno power header: 5V and the first GND. The image shows the first GND pin, which I took as GND.1.
Every plug-in connection gets both a joined edge and an electrical edge on the same ports.
